reason: Full-source review found the query inventory itself accurate. The candidate correctly covers non-archived customers, monthly event counts, invoice and line-item aggregation, daily draft snapshots, global-maximum snapshot selection, ID-plus-snapshot breakdown joins, Production-only breakdown examples, exclusion of negative aggregate line items, archived contracts, descending override ordering without a one-row limit, future-ending rate-card entries, active webhook-alert predicates, and alert-history grouping. It also correctly identifies three defects in the raw cookbook: the Finalized Invoices queries have no status predicate although the database reference says invoice contains both FINALIZED and VOID rows; the query titled over the last week has no time predicate; and the detailed draft-breakdown query selects six nonaggregated expressions while grouping by only two despite the standard-SQL framing. Its universal-divide-by-100 caution is directionally correct. Approval is nevertheless blocked by material table-grain and aggregation omissions exposed by the already-ingested export authorities. Metronome configures one export destination across Production and Sandbox, but outside the two breakdown examples most cookbook queries do not filter environment_type; their counts and monetary totals therefore cannot be presented as environment-scoped without an explicit filter. Object-storage exports are append-only and at-least-once and incremental consumers must resolve repeated primary keys to the latest row, yet none of the cookbook queries performs delivery deduplication. A global maximum snapshot_time or snapshot_timestamp is also not a per-object latest-row or completeness guarantee. The draft_invoice reference permits DRAFT_INCOMPLETE rows with no total or line items, so COUNT can include incomplete invoices while SUM ignores null totals unless status/completeness is handled. The active-rate-card-entry query checks only ending_before greater than NOW(): it does not check starting_at, does not define how nullable ending_before behaves, and does not select among version or snapshot rows, so it is not a complete active-entry count. The candidate's generic lifecycle and duplicate-handling sentence is too weak for these documented cross-source boundaries, while the proposed query-patterns update would canonize the patterns without their necessary environment, deduplication, incomplete-draft, and version-selection qualifications. Finally, total/100 is not a universal fiat conversion under the existing Metronome currency authority, but the candidate and shared update do not link that direct authority. Mechanical checks pass: the trusted raw SHA-256, canonical URL, raw_files value, source target state, and exact path-qualified raw backlink are correct; no duplicate canonical source exists; candidate.md equals receipt.source_page; suggestions.json equals receipt.suggestions; all five grounding excerpts byte-match their cited raw spans; and the selected reporting concept is the correct authority. These semantic and cross-source corrections require another full-source review.
required_changes: Add an explicit environment-scope caution to the candidate and reporting concept update. The export overview says one destination spans Production and Sandbox, while only the two draft-breakdown examples add environment_type = 'PRODUCTION'. State that the other cookbook counts and totals are not environment-scoped as written, and require the intended per-table environment predicate before interpreting them as production metrics.

Carry the documented delivery and draft-grain boundaries into the candidate and shared cautions. Object-storage exports are append-only and at-least-once, so repeated primary keys from updates or retries require latest-row resolution before aggregation; a global maximum snapshot is not a substitute for per-key deduplication or a per-object completeness guarantee. The draft_invoice reference also permits DRAFT_INCOMPLETE rows with no total or line items, so explain that COUNT may include incomplete rows while SUM ignores null totals unless status and completeness are handled.

Strengthen the contracts/rate-card qualification. Keep the correct observation that descending updated_at does not return only one override. Also state that the query titled active rate-card entries checks only ending_before > NOW(), omits starting_at, does not define nullable ending_before handling, and does not select among version or snapshot rows; do not present it as a complete current-state count without reconciling the database-reference grain.

Retain the total/100 warning but link the direct denomination authority, [[metronome-currencies-and-custom-pricing-units]] and/or [[source-metronome-guides-pricing-packaging-make-pricing-changes-use-currency-custompricingunits]]. Preserve that Metronome documents USD API values in cents but listed non-USD fiat in whole units, so the cookbook alias total_dollars cannot establish a universal divide-by-100 rule. Keep this separate from export delivery and invoice-status concerns.

Update data-export-cookbook-query-patterns and data-export-cookbook-query-contradictions so their canonical prose includes the environment, at-least-once deduplication, DRAFT_INCOMPLETE, and rate-card version/effective-time boundaries above. Retain the existing finalized-versus-void, missing-seven-day-filter, and strict-grouping warnings. The reciprocal source link can be approved only after its status, snapshot, aggregation, and currency description points to corrected concept content.

Its three listed SQL defects are valid, but the canonical caution omits the material Production-versus-Sandbox aggregation risk, repeated-primary-key delivery risk, incomplete-draft count-versus-sum boundary, and incomplete active-rate-card predicate.

The reciprocal citation is warranted after correction, but its snapshot, aggregation, and currency description must point to concept prose carrying the complete documented boundaries and direct currency authority.
